reflection_nebula.notes: Subtlety is everything. Blue reflection color must be preserved. Over-processing destroys the delicate dust structure. NXT must be very gentle. Brighter background needed to reveal faint nebulosity. BRIGHT-CORE reflection nebulae (e.g. NGC 7023 Iris around HD 200775): SXT mis-extracts the bright central glow as a large diffuse 'star' blob — re-adding it (with star-stretch+saturation) looks strange. Use star_protected_blend with aggressive core protection (min_strength_fraction ~0.0, core_threshold_low/high ~0.55/0.70) so the blob is NOT re-added; the starless retains the core glow. SURROUNDING IFN: the Iris is embedded in a large BROWN dark molecular cloud (LDN 1174) that should be clearly visible filling the frame — warm tan dust with dark patches, NOT a black background. Lift shadows / raise background, and PRESERVE the warm brown dust color (do not let the IFN go grey/neutral or crush to black). Reference look: structured blue reflection core with brown dust lanes threading into the bright center, surrounded by brown IFN everywhere.

narrowband_palette.description: OVERLAY (not a target class): deep-merged over the target-class profile when the workflow is SHO/HOO (mono S/H/O masters, false-color palette).

SPCC.reason: False-color palette: no photometric white point. Color is set by sho_combine + sho_hue_shift.

SCNR.reason: Only as a final touch on residual green; prefer sho_hue_shift, which moves Ha-green to gold instead of greying it.

LRGB.reason: Use Ha (or 0.7H+0.3O synthetic) as luminance for detail when the palette mix softens structure.

Ha_injection.reason: Ha already IS a palette channel.

NXT.reason: Per-channel NXT read by narrowband-prep.mjs (previously hardcoded in code and the 0.25/0.30 scalars here were ignored). SII is the weakest channel and gets the largest palette gain, so it needs the most post-stretch denoise.

palette.goal: Hubble look: gold/orange Ha-dominant body, cyan-blue OIII cavities/edges, red-orange SII accents. Green < 10% of subject pixels, magenta < 8%. Neutral dark background.

core_burn._calibration: 2026-10-27 back-test on the USER-APPROVED PACMAN LIFT5: the brightest zone in an SHO palette is the OIII cavity, a naturally smooth glow (relContrast 0.055, white/desat clauses pass). The default 0.22 rejected the approved image, so it was wrong for palettes. 0.03 still catches a completely featureless core.

halo_lift.reason: USER-APPROVED (PACMAN LIFT5 'really perfect'): the unlinked stretch + contrast curve crushes the faint outer Ha nebulosity. Reveal it through a body-excluding mask, give it the palette's gold, sharpen the body edge. Tools: lift_faint_halo then body_edge_contrast.
